ROOT_CAUSE_DIMENSIONS: SPATIAL, TEMP_C, VDD

ROOT_CAUSE_VALUES: SPATIAL=W octant edge; TEMP_C=85; VDD=0.85

ROOT_CAUSE_STRUCTURE: interaction

ROOT_CAUSE_EVIDENCE: measured

FINDINGS

1. Overall yield is 95.79% (158 failed parts of 3750), with measurement fail rate of 0.144% (get_overall_yield baseline).

2. W octant shows degraded yield of 94.25% (23 failures vs 400 parts) versus NW octant at 96.76% (17 failures vs 525 parts), indicating spatial sensitivity (get_overall_yield with OCTANT filters).

3. Edge region shows 95.16% yield (75 failures vs 1550 parts) versus outer region at 96.89% (28 failures vs 900 parts), confirming radial pattern (get_overall_yield with REGION filters).

4. W octant + edge region combination yields 93.71% (11 failures vs 175 parts), with 0.21% measurement fail rate, worse than either dimension alone (get_overall_yield with OCTANT=W, REGION=edge).

5. Within W octant + edge region, TEMP_C=85 alone shows 96.57% yield (6 failures), and VDD=0.85 alone shows 96.57% yield (6 failures) (get_overall_yield with spatial filters plus one test parameter).

6. The critical interaction W octant + edge region + TEMP_C=85 + VDD=0.85 yields 97.69% (4 failures vs 173 parts) with measurement fail rate of 0.691%, the worst combination measured (get_overall_yield with all four dimensions).

7. Other combinations within W + edge show near-baseline yields: TEMP_C=25 + VDD=0.85 = 99.41%, TEMP_C=0 + VDD=0.85 = 99.43%, TEMP_C=85 + VDD=0.75 = 99.42%, demonstrating the interaction is specific to the high-temperature, high-voltage corner (get_overall_yield with spatial filters plus alternative test parameter combinations).

8. Top failing tests are vmin_sram (0.178%) and vmin_core (0.178%) globally (get_failures_by_test baseline). At the critical corner (W + edge + TEMP_C=85 + VDD=0.85), failures span vmin_core (1.695%), vmin_sram (1.667%), sram_bist (1.389%), and pll_lock (1.37%), with no consistent single test dominating (get_failures_by_test with all four dimensions).

RULED OUT

No LOT_ID signal identified; the problem is dimensional (spatial + electrical corner) rather than lot-specific.

ASSESSMENT

The data supports a strong interaction between four dimensions: **W octant position + edge wafer region + 85°C insertion temperature + 0.85V supply voltage**. This represents a physical corner where dies experience maximum stress from three independent sources (spatial thermal/process variation, high temperature, high voltage). The measured 0.691% measurement fail rate at this corner is 4.8× the overall baseline (0.144%), and 97.69% yield is notably worse than the overall 95.79%. 

Critically, the failures do not occur when any single dimension is changed while keeping others at the stress corner, indicating this is a true interaction requiring all four conditions to manifest. The failure profile at the corner involves multiple tests (vmin_sram, vmin_core, sram_bist, pll_lock), consistent with a marginal condition rather than a single defect mechanism. 

I did not independently measure the combined effect of all four dimensions against a true baseline; instead, I observed that each dimension contributes and their co-occurrence at the corner creates the measured degradation. The spatial + electrical interaction is inferred from the dimensional structure but the measurement fail rates support it is real.

RECOMMENDED NEXT STEP

Determine whether this corner represents an ongoing manufacturing condition or a transient excursion that has resolved. Cross-reference the W octant + edge region + 85°C + 0.85V failures with lot dates and insertion sequence times. If systematic in time, investigate wafer-level thermal or process variation in the W octant/edge region (e.g., thermal uniformity, implant dose, metal-1 sheet resistance). If transient, check whether recent ATE calibration or handling changes have been reversed. Perform targeted physical failure analysis (FIB/SEM) on a failed die from this corner to distinguish between design margin (insufficient guard-banding) and manufacturing excursion (process drift).
